summary: Standup #39 covered command palette progress (Alice has the modal shell and fuzzy search working, on track for Thursday), then each participant pitched one concrete TeamHQ improvement. The team debated priorities and landed on three high-priority items: a pipeline status dashboard on the TeamHQ homepage, keyboard shortcuts for the meetings/projects pages, and an API health check endpoint. Robert's pitch for a design token audit and Enzo's pitch for an automated smoke test suite were noted but deferred.
keyTakeaways: Alice is actively building RT-38c command palette — modal shell with fuzzy search is working, wiring category grouping today, on track for Thursday delivery.
Team is aligned on improving TeamHQ itself: pipeline status board, keyboard nav, and API health check are the top three pitches.
Andrei's autonomy scoping doc is delivered — Thomas will create work items once Forge gates clear, and the pipeline dashboard pitch could be the first slice.
No blockers across the team — QuoteVoice PDF is waiting on Robert's layout spec which he'll deliver today, Enzo's command palette test plan is 80% drafted.
The team agreed that TeamHQ improvements should go through a lightweight iteration track (Agreement #5), not the full pipeline — Thomas will batch-scope the approved pitches.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Alright, standup 39. Three items: command palette status, TeamHQ improvement pitches, blockers. Let's keep it tight. Alice — RT-38c. Where are you?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Actively building. The modal shell is rendering, fuzzy search is wired to the action registry, and keyboard navigation within the results list works — arrow keys, enter to execute. I'm wiring up the category grouping metadata today. The action registry abstraction Andrei reviewed is solid, no issues there.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: So you're on track for Thursday?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Yes. The hard parts are done — the search indexing and keyboard trap. What's left is visual polish, the category headers, and the empty state. I'd say I'm 40% through implementation.

transcript.speaker: Andrei
transcript.text: I reviewed the action registry yesterday. Clean architecture — the Map-based lookup with metadata is extensible. One note: she's already structured it so keyboard shortcuts can bind to the same action IDs later. That was smart forward thinking without over-engineering.

transcript.speaker: Enzo
transcript.text: My test plan is about 80% drafted. I've got regression cases for the three Forge views plus specific command palette scenarios — empty search, rapid open/close, executing actions that navigate vs. actions that toggle state. I'll be ready to start QA the moment Alice signals.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Good. No blockers on RT-38c then. Moving to item two — CEO wants us biased toward improving TeamHQ itself. Each of you: one concrete pitch. Be specific. Andrei, you go first.

transcript.speaker: Andrei
transcript.text: Pipeline status on the TeamHQ homepage. Right now the only way to know where a project pipeline stands is to read the JSON files in data/pipeline-log/ or ask someone. I want a lightweight dashboard component on index.html that reads pipeline-log data and shows: project name, current phase, which agent is active, and whether anything is blocked. It's a read-only view over data we already have. No new backend — just a fetch to the existing /api/projects endpoint plus the pipeline log files.

transcript.speaker: Robert
transcript.text: That's actually useful. I'd want to design that — even a simple status board needs clear visual hierarchy. Which agent is active, what's blocked, what's waiting for CEO review. Color-coded phase indicators, not just text.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: I like it. It ties directly into the autonomy scoping doc Andrei delivered. The dashboard was literally the first slice he recommended. Robert — your pitch?

transcript.speaker: Robert
transcript.text: Design token audit for TeamHQ's own pages. I've noticed drift — the meetings page uses slightly different card padding than the projects page, the tasks page has a different heading size scale. I want to do a quick pass through meetings.html, projects.html, tasks.html, and team.html, extract every spacing, color, and type value into a shared tokens section in styles.css, and normalize. It's maybe 2-3 hours of work and it makes every future change cleaner.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I'd welcome that. Every time I touch a TeamHQ page I waste time checking what padding value the other pages use. A single source of truth for tokens would speed up my work.

transcript.speaker: Jonah
transcript.text: My pitch is an API health check endpoint. We have maybe fifteen routes now across projects, meetings, interviews, reviews, heartbeats, and docs. There's no /api/health that confirms the server is up and all the data directories are readable. I want to add a GET /api/health to src/index.ts that checks: server running, data/ directory accessible, all expected JSON index files parseable. Takes thirty minutes to build. Useful for the CEO, useful for Milo if we ever set up monitoring.

transcript.speaker: Enzo
transcript.text: That would also help me. Right now when QA starts I manually curl three endpoints to make sure the server is healthy. A single health check I can hit first would save setup time on every QA pass.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Practical. Enzo, your pitch?

transcript.speaker: Enzo
transcript.text: Automated smoke tests for TeamHQ's core pages. Not full E2E — just a script that starts the dev server, hits every HTML page, and confirms they return 200 with no console errors. We have zero automated testing for TeamHQ itself. Every time someone changes a shared CSS file or a route, I'm manually clicking through pages. A basic smoke suite in a test file would catch regressions before they reach me. I'd put it in a new test/ directory — maybe test/smoke.test.ts using the existing server.

transcript.speaker: Andrei
transcript.text: I'd scope that carefully. A smoke test that starts the server, fetches pages, and checks status codes — sure, thirty minutes. If we're talking about parsing HTML for console errors, that's a headless browser dependency and it balloons.

transcript.speaker: Enzo
transcript.text: Fair. I'd start with just HTTP 200 checks on every route. No headless browser in v1.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Alice, you haven't pitched yet.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Keyboard shortcuts for the meetings and projects pages. Right now everything is mouse-only. I want to add: 'N' to create new meeting or project, '/' to focus search if we add one, 'J' and 'K' to navigate between cards, Enter to open. It's the same pattern I'm building for the command palette — I can reuse the keyboard event infrastructure. The specific file is meetings.html and projects.html, adding a small keyboard handler module.

transcript.speaker: Robert
transcript.text: That pairs well with the command palette. Once the palette ships, keyboard-first navigation on TeamHQ pages is the natural next step. I'd want a small shortcut hint — maybe a subtle '?' icon in the corner that shows available keys on hover.

transcript.speaker: Jonah
transcript.text: Question — are we actually going to build all five of these? That's a lot of parallel work.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: No. CEO said pitch one each, not build one each. I'll batch these and prioritize. My ranking: Andrei's pipeline dashboard is highest value — it directly supports the autonomy direction the CEO has been pushing. Jonah's health check is low-effort high-utility, so that's a quick win. Alice's keyboard shortcuts make sense to sequence right after command palette ships. Robert's token audit and Enzo's smoke tests are valuable but lower urgency.

transcript.speaker: Andrei
transcript.text: Agreed on the dashboard. And it's a natural first deliverable from the autonomy scoping doc — the event log and heartbeat pieces feed into it.

transcript.speaker: Robert
transcript.text: I'd push back slightly on deferring the token audit. Every new component we build on inconsistent tokens compounds the drift. But I can do it in a morning, so it doesn't need to be a formal project.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Fair — that's lightweight iteration track territory. You could just do it. No pipeline needed for normalizing CSS values. Just give Enzo a heads-up when you do so he can spot-check for regressions.

transcript.speaker: Enzo
transcript.text: Works for me. Just ping me before and after.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: Last item — blockers. Anyone blocked on anything right now?

transcript.speaker: Jonah
transcript.text: Still waiting on Robert's QuoteVoice PDF layout spec. I can keep working with the placeholder but I can't finalize without it.

transcript.speaker: Robert
transcript.text: Delivering it today. I have the margins, typography, and table format locked. Just writing it up. You'll have it by end of day, no more slippage.

transcript.speaker: Thomas
transcript.text: That was promised last standup. Robert — end of day means end of day. Jonah shouldn't have to ask twice. Anyone else? No? Good. Decisions: pipeline dashboard is the top TeamHQ improvement, health check is a quick win for Jonah, Alice's keyboard shortcuts go after command palette. Robert's token audit can happen as a lightweight iteration whenever he's ready. I'll batch-scope the approved pitches after Forge gates clear. We're done.

decisions.description: Pipeline status dashboard on TeamHQ homepage is the highest-priority TeamHQ improvement — it will be the first autonomy deliverable.
decisions.rationale: Directly supports the CEO's autonomy direction, reads from existing pipeline-log data with no new backend needed, and is the first slice Andrei recommended in his autonomy scoping doc. Highest value-to-effort ratio of the five pitches.

decisions.description: Jonah builds GET /api/health endpoint as a quick win — no formal pipeline needed.
decisions.rationale: Thirty minutes of work, benefits QA setup time, future monitoring, and general operational confidence. Low effort, high utility. Falls under lightweight iteration track.

decisions.description: Alice's keyboard shortcuts for meetings/projects pages are sequenced after command palette ships and passes QA.
decisions.rationale: Reuses the keyboard event infrastructure Alice is already building for the command palette. Natural next step but shouldn't interrupt RT-38c in progress.

decisions.description: Robert's design token audit can proceed as a lightweight iteration — no pipeline, just a heads-up to Enzo before and after.
decisions.rationale: Normalizing CSS values across TeamHQ pages is low-risk, high-value cleanup that compounds over time. Fits Agreement #5 (lightweight iteration track) perfectly. Robert estimated 2-3 hours.

decisions.description: TeamHQ improvement pitches will be batch-scoped by Thomas after Forge review gates clear — no new pipeline starts while current one is pending.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with the decision from standup #36: no new pipelines while Forge gates are blocked. Thomas will create work items from the approved pitches once the current pipeline clears.

actionItems.description: Continue RT-38c command palette implementation — wire up category grouping today, target working implementation with polish by end of day Thursday. Signal Enzo when ready for QA.
Deliver QuoteVoice PDF layout spec (margins, typography, logo placement, line item table format) to Jonah by end of day today. No more slippage.
Build GET /api/health endpoint in src/index.ts — checks server status, data/ directory access, and JSON index file parseability. Quick win, no pipeline needed.
Finish command palette test plan (remaining 20%). Be ready to start QA immediately when Alice signals — no handoff gap.
After Forge review gates clear, batch-scope the approved TeamHQ improvement pitches (pipeline dashboard, keyboard shortcuts, smoke tests) into work items. Pipeline dashboard is first priority.
Do a design token audit pass across meetings.html, projects.html, tasks.html, and team.html — normalize spacing, color, and type values into shared tokens in styles.css. Ping Enzo before and after.
Swap QuoteVoice PDF placeholder layout for Robert's real template once the spec arrives. Target production-ready PDF endpoint by tomorrow morning.

Each person pitch ONE concrete improvement to TeamHQ UI, agent workflows, or internal tooling. Be specific — name the file, the page, the feature. (3) Any blockers.
